As R increases beyond 0.7, C degrades significantly due to inefficient talent allocation. Simultaneously, taxpayer subsidies (S) create fiscal externalities that distort local economies, with E = g(S). These two variables interact through regulatory frameworks—where M = 1 (artificial monopoly), antitrust scrutiny intensifies. The economic model assumes that sports do not meet natural monopoly criteria, implying that legal exemptions should be scrutinized. Thus, the system exhibits dual failure modes: allocative inefficiency (R) and fiscal misalignment (S), both of which can be modeled using Bayesian inference in GSI and simulated in GSE.
